NUMBER 9 OF 2023

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

Empowerment and Protection of women currently need to receive serious attention from all parties, including attention from the Regional Government, related to the existence of phenomena in social community life that often victimizes them due to violence and exploitation, they are often positioned as economic objects and often marginalized and/or excluded in social interactions.

In Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence (Domestic Violence Law), it is stipulated that the state guarantees the prevention of domestic violence, prosecution of perpetrators of domestic violence, and protection of victims of domestic violence. Victims of domestic violence, who are mostly women and children, must receive protection to be prevented from and freed from violence or threats of violence, torture, or treatment that demeans their dignity and human worth. Therefore, the Regional Government makes regulations related to Women's Empowerment and Protection.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 19

Further provisions regarding prevention of violence against women as referred to in Articles 16, 17 and 18 shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 18

Prevention of violence against women is carried out in an integrated and coordinated manner between those responsible for prevention of violence against women and Regional Apparatus that oversee women empowerment and child protection affairs.

Article 39

(1) The community participates in the implementation of women's empowerment and protection.

(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be in the form of:

a. providing education on women's rights; b. providing skills training to support the community's economy;
c. establishing community social institutions to assist victims of violence;
d. providing information and/or reporting violence against women to law enforcement or authorities; and/or
b. participating in handling acts of violence against women.

Article 1

In this regional regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is Mamuju Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Government of Mamuju Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Mamuju.
4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is an auxiliary element of the regional head and DPRD in organizing government affairs that are the authority of the region.
5. Women's empowerment is every effort to improve physical, mental spiritual, social, knowledge and skills abilities so that women are ready to be utilized in accordance with their respective capabilities.
6. Protection of Women is all efforts made by families, government and others directed at women to ensure the fulfillment of women's rights as a form of respect for human rights.
7. Discrimination against women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, which has the effect or purpose of diminishing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women.
8. Violence Against Women is any action that violates, hinders, eliminates enjoyment, and neglects women's human rights.
9. Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an integrated service center in the efforts to organize women in various fields of development, as well as protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the government or community-based.
10. Integrated Service Unit hereinafter abbreviated as UPT is technical service units in the regions that carry out integrated service functions for women and children victims of crime and/or violence, including as an information center for organizing women and child protection.
11. Gender is a concept that refers to the differentiation of roles, functions and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
12. Gender Mainstreaming, hereinafter abbreviated as PUG, is a strategy built to integrate gender into men and women.
13. Regional Action Plan for Gender Mainstreaming hereinafter referred to as RANDA PUG is a planning document as a guideline in efforts to implement development strategies by integrating gender into one integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of policies, programs, and development activities in the region.
14. PUG Institution is an institution that meets the elements of PUG prerequisites, which functions effectively in a sustainable system with agreed norms in fulfilling the human rights of women and men fairly to achieve equality between women and men in all fields of development and levels of government.
15. Community institutions are institutions formed by members of the Indonesian citizen community voluntarily on the basis of a shared vision, mission, profession, function, and activities to participate in development in order to achieve national goals within the framework of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila, consisting of religious organizations, non-governmental organizations, professional organizations, private organizations, social organizations, political organizations, mass media, and other forms of organizations.
16. Victim is a person who experiences violence and/or threat of violence within the scope of the household. 17. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations. 18. Task force is a coordinative institution formed by the Government of Mamuju Regency that coordinates policies, programs and activities for the protection of women and children in Mamuju Regency.

Article 2

(1) The Regional Government has obligations and responsibilities towards the empowerment and Protection of Women. (2) The efforts of Empowerment and Protection of Women as referred to in paragraph (1) include:

a. determination of policies, programs, and activities; b. determination of implementation guidelines;
c. provision of services; and
b. coordination of policies, programs and activities. (3) The efforts of Empowerment and Protection of Women as referred to in paragraph (2) are carried out in an integrated manner in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.

Article 26

(1) Health services as referred to in Article 24 paragraph (1) letter b shall be implemented with the following activities:

a. physical and mental health examination and care; b. psychological examination and recovery;
c. pregnancy, childbirth, and reproductive health services;
d. medical resume and psychological examination results; e. visum et repertum and visum et psikiatrikum; f. Deoxyribonucleic Acid test; and
g. other forms of health services needed by victims.

(4) Further provisions regarding health services shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND PROTECTION

I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

Empowerment and Protection of women currently need to receive serious attention from all parties, including attention from the Regional Government, related to the existence of phenomena in social community life that often victimizes them due to violence and exploitation, they are often positioned as economic objects and often marginalized and/or excluded in social interactions.

In Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence (Domestic Violence Law), it is stipulated that the state guarantees the prevention of domestic violence, prosecution of perpetrators of domestic violence, and protection of victims of domestic violence. Victims of domestic violence, who are mostly women and children, must receive protection to be prevented from and freed from violence or threats of violence, torture, or treatment that demeans their dignity and human worth. Therefore, the Regional Government makes regulations related to Women's Empowerment and Protection.

PROTECTION OF WOMEN

Article 11

(1) Women's empowerment in the field of law as referred to in Article 9 letter b includes:

a. increasing awareness and knowledge in the field of law through communication, information and education services;
b. mapping and review of gender-biased policies; and c. facilitation of access and legal consultation services. (2) Women's empowerment in the field of law as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.

Article 10

(1) Women's empowerment in the field of politics as referred to in Article 9 letter a includes:

a. involvement of women in decision-making at various levels;
b. provision of opportunities for women to hold public office;
c. participation in general elections; and
d. self-development through organizations to associate, assemble and express opinions.
(2) Women's empowerment in the field of politics as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.
(3) The Regional Government provides guarantees to women to elect and/or be elected in: a. general elections;
b. regional head elections;
c. village head elections; and/or
d. elections for other political positions. based on equal rights.
(4) Equal rights as referred to in Paragraph (3) shall be implemented through direct, general, free, secret, honest and fair voting according to the applicable laws and regulations.
(5) The Regional Government provides opportunities for women to be appointed as regional government officials and occupy strategic positions in regional government; and
(6) The Regional Government and/or Political Parties are responsible for providing political education for women.

Article 7

(1) In an effort to accelerate the institutionalization of PUG as referred to in Article 4 paragraph (1) letter b, a PUG working group is established.

(2) Members of the PUG working group are all heads/leaders of PD. (3) The Regent establishes:

a. the head of the PD that administers governmental affairs in the field of regional development planning as the chairman of the PUG working group; and
b. the head of the PD that administers governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection as the head of the secretariat of the PUG working group.
(4) The establishment of the PUG working group as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be stipulated by Regent's Decree.
